question.text: A portfolio manager makes 40 independent predictions per year with an Information Coefficient of 0.15. What is her Information Ratio (IR), rounded to two decimals?

explanation.text: The Logic: Fundamental Law of Active Management: IR = IC × √Breadth = 0.15 × √40 = 0.15 × 6.3246 ≈ 0.95. IR rises linearly with IC and only with the square root of breadth. The Trap: 6.00 is just √40 without multiplying by IC; 0.15 is the raw IC; 2.37 comes from mis-applying the formula. Note: The IC effect is linear; the breadth effect is non-linear (square root). Increasing predictions improves IR only by the square root.
